S1Result: Five accessibility regressions. One app. Four test suites.
The test ID suite caught none of them. Every test stayed green.
The ARIA snapshot suite caught all five.
The suite that survives change best also notices least. Here is why.
S2Setup: The testbed is a small task board app. It has seven user scenarios.
Each scenario is written four ways. CSS selectors. Test IDs. Role locators. And ARIA snapshots.
The snapshot suite acts through role locators. But every assertion is a short template of the accessibility tree.
S3Regressions: Then I seeded five regressions into the app. One per build.
A heading drops from level two to level four. A list becomes plain divs. A button becomes a clickable div. An alert loses its role. A label loses its input.
On screen every build looks the same as the original. Only the accessibility tree changes.
S4Blind: The test ID suite finds elements by a private attribute. The demoted heading keeps that attribute.
So the locator still matches. The text still says My Tasks. The test passes.
With all five regressions in one build the test ID suite still ran seven of seven green. It never looks at what users get.
S5Caught: The snapshot template records more than a name. It records the role and the heading level.
Expected level two. Received level four. The test fails with a diff you can read.
A role locator for the heading named My Tasks matches a level four heading too. So the role locator suite missed this one.
Final count. CSS selectors caught one. Test IDs caught none. Role locators caught four. ARIA snapshots caught all five.
S6Cost: Breadth has a cost. After a redesign the snapshot suite passed three of seven. Test IDs passed six.
A snapshot asserts the whole subtree it covers. So any change inside that subtree fails the test.
The update is one command. Playwright writes a patch file for you to review. It does not edit your test file.
Apply the patch and fix two locators. The suite then passed the redesign and a later migration with no other changes.
S7Dial: Survival and vigilance sit on one dial. Test IDs sit at one end. Whole page snapshots sit at the other.
The templates here were scoped and partial. Wider templates would break more often and catch more. Where you set that dial is the real decision.
One caveat. The app is small and I wrote the regressions myself. Run the suites against your own app before you trust the numbers.
S8EndCard: Every suite and every number is in the public repo. The links are in the description.
